samples.summary: Read-only notes mounts are enforced only by `EditorView.editable`; the notes engine has no `EditorState.readOnly` and no read-only store wrapper, and this change widens that surface for viewer-role share links
samples.evidence: `initialize()` implements read-only as `EditorView.editable.of(!readOnly)` (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:425) plus hiding mutating API surface. `EditorState.readOnly` is never set (only in a test, checkbox-input.test.ts:87), and `noteSync` forwards ANY non-remote transaction carrying a `input`/`delete`/`move` user event straight to the store -> `YorkieNoteStore.editText()` -> Yorkie CRDT write (packages/notes/src/view/note-sync.ts:57-100). There is no notes equivalent of `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts`, whose own doc comment states the reason this matters: "the server-side check behind it — the Yorkie auth webhook — ships in shadow mode by default (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE`), so with the default configuration this flag is the write boundary rather than a convenience in front of one" (read-only.ts:35-42); the backend confirms the default (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:100-101, self-hosting.md:185 `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE | false`). Vector: a visitor holding a *viewer*-role note share link opens the page and, from the console, dispatches into the mounted CodeMirror view (`EditorView.findFromDOM(...).dispatch({changes, userEvent:'input'})`) or calls the `NoteEditorAPI` mutators; noteSync writes it to the shared document, and in a stock deployment the webhook is in shadow mode so the server allows it. The change under review expands exactly this surface: `shared-notes-layout.tsx:117` now passes `onEditorReady={setEditor}` on the viewer mount (the old code passed none, so no external handle to the mutating API existed on that route) and the new view menu lets a viewer leave the preview-only pane for the editor pane (`shared-notes-layout.tsx:49-51,84-86`), which the previous code hard-pinned to `viewMode: "view"`. I could not find a *click-only* (no-devtools) write path in the read-only mount — the checkbox input checks `EditorView.editable` and the preview's `onToggleTask` is undefined when readOnly — hence medium rather than high confidence.
searchedFor: glob packages/notes/src/store/*.ts + grep readOnly there (no matches)

samples.summary: Fail-open role comparison: anything that is not exactly the string "viewer" is treated as an editor, granting the formatting toolbar and the share-token image uploader
samples.evidence: `const readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer";` (shared-notes-layout.tsx:44) is a deny-list over a field typed as bare `string` (packages/frontend/src/api/share-links.ts:16, echoed verbatim from the DB by share-link.controller.ts:72). Any other value ('', 'commenter', a future 'reviewer' role, a legacy row) yields readOnly=false, which mounts the full formatting group and constructs `shareTokenImageUploader(token)` (line 73-76) for a link that was never meant to write. An allow-list (`role !== "editor"`) fails closed instead. Not exploitable today: `ShareLinkService.create` rejects any role outside viewer|editor (share-link.service.ts:77-81) and both the upload route (image-share-upload.controller.ts:135) and the Yorkie webhook (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:217) require `role === 'editor'` server-side, so the backend fails closed. Reporting the shape because the line was relocated into a new module and is now the gate for a newly-added write capability (image upload).

samples.summary: The "Show authors" blame-gutter toggle is now offered to anonymous and viewer-role visitors, including the public, unauthenticated template preview at /t/:id
samples.evidence: The toolbar is mounted for readOnly visitors too and the `Show authors` item sits outside the `!readOnly` gate (notes-toolbar.tsx:626-634), wired to `onShowAuthorsChange={setShowAuthors}` here (line 111). Before this change the shared mount passed no `showAuthors`, so the gutter appeared only if the *visitor's own* browser had `wafflebase:notes:showAuthors=true` — effectively never for an internet visitor. `template-landing.tsx:174` mounts `SharedDocumentByToken` on a listing's public `previewToken` (minted with role 'viewer', template.service.ts:374), so an unauthenticated visitor to a published note template can now surface the workspace members' recorded display names in one click. Likely accepted rather than a defect: `yorkie-note-store.ts:52-58` documents that author attributes live in the note content and are "readable by anyone who can read the note at all, including anonymous viewer-role share-link visitors", and the names ship in the CRDT payload the client already receives — so this is a UI surfacing, not a new data channel. Note in passing that `notes-settings.ts:41-45` still claims the toggle also controls whether the visitor's own name is recorded, which `yorkie-note-store.ts:44-50` contradicts (recording is unconditional).

verdict.reason: Verified independently: the notes engine's read-only mode is only `EditorView.editable.of(!readOnly)` (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:425) plus feature-omission (uploadImage, onToggleTask, historyKeymap). `EditorState.readOnly` is never set in packages/notes/src outside tests (checkbox-input.test.ts:87), and there is no changeFilter/transactionFilter anywhere in the engine. `noteSync` forwards any non-remote transaction with an input/delete/move user event into `store.editText()` with no editable/readOnly consultation (note-sync.ts:57-66, 89-100), and none of the NoteEditorAPI mutators or view/commands.ts check editability (grep for `editable|readOnly` in commands.ts: no matches), so `editor.toggleBold()` / a console `view.dispatch(...)` writes to the CRDT on a read-only mount. There is no notes analogue of the docs read-only store wrapper: repo-wide grep for `readOnly*Store` yields only packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:67 (used at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1075), while packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:136-139 hands `initialize()` a raw `YorkieNoteStore` even when readOnly. The server-side backstop is shadow mode by default — yorkie-auth.controller.ts:100-101 and 111-119 return ALLOW unless YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE==='true', documented as default `false` (self-hosting.md:185, backend/README.md:101) — and the shared note mount attaches a normal DocumentProvider with no read-only sync mode (shared-document.tsx:989-1003). The change under review does widen the surface (shared-notes-layout.tsx:117 passes onEditorReady on the viewer mount; :49-51,84-86 let a viewer leave the preview-only pane). This is an authorization weakness in lane (viewer-role write boundary bypassable in a stock deployment); no counterexample found.
